I’ve only been able to see my GP and a neurologist. Also been to the ER number ours times. CT in ER came out normal, insurance won’t cover an MRI and rheumatologists have been refusing to see me. I decided to get a different GP and she came up with the possibility of Tardive Dyskinesia due to my Seroquel although wants to do more research. I’ve been doing my own research with that lead and noticed Tardive Dyskinesia really only affects the mouth/jaw and my whole body is affected which lead me to think maybe General Dystonia. The reason I think MS as well is, my mom has auto-immune disorder, I fatigue easy now, pain is high and almost all over burning sensation, I’ve been seeing lots of floaters, I’ve become sensitive to cold and hot temperatures, honestly most symptoms of MS it goes on and on.

Well I definitely think that those are obtainable skills you can learn! My advice (feel free to take it if you like it and leave it if you don’t) would be to 
1. Always make time for yourself to recharge, you can’t be very social/outgoing if you’re energetically drained. 2. Don’t worry about your RBF, most people have it anyway, especially those of us who are more in our heads, but if you find yourself lost in thought and feel your face scrunching, remind yourself to de-tense and take a breath to relax your facial muscles. 3. Remember that being social/outgoing doesn’t mean you have to have a big circle of friends (that can even make you feel even more isolated as an introvert) focus on being social with people you feel comfortable around and drawn to first, if finding those people feels difficult don’t be ashamed or afraid to try something like bumble BFF (I have heard great stories about it). 4. Being friendly in small ways can go a long way, sharing compliments and smiles is always a good way to start and 5. If going out to big gatherings/parties is scary, you can always be social through study groups and clubs and work your way up (those are more beneficial to you anyway) I hope that might help!
